ORDER Appellant/claimant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 assailing the impugned award dated 12/10/2018 passed by 6th Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Morena in Claims Case No. 115/2017; whereby, though Claims Tribunal found appellant/claimant entitled for a compensation of Rs. 99,763/- but rejected the claim of appellant while observing that appellant failed to prove factum of accident by the offending vehicle.

sentences.text:
Briefly stated facts of the case are that as per the claim case, on 27/10/2016 when appellant alongwith his son Jitendra was going on motorcycle to Jitendra's in-law's house and as soon as they reached on road, it is alleged that due to rash and negligent driving of motor cycle No.
MP06HJ8909 by its driver/respondent No. 1, said motorcycle dashed the motorcycle of appellant and in said accident, appellant sustained injuries in right leg below knee and also sustained multiple fractures, which gave rise to filing of claim case by the appellant seeking total compensation of Rs.
15,20,000/-; however, learned Claims Tribunal by the impugned award though found the appellant entitled to receive a compensation of Rs. 99,763/- however, rejected the claim of appellant on the ground that appellant failed to prove the factum of accident by the offending motorcycle and therefore, respondents were exonerated from the liability.

3. It is the submission of learned counsel for the appellant that learned Claims Tribunal erred in rejecting the claim case of appellant ignoring the evidence brought on record documentary as well as oral.
In hospital, the appellant given the cause of sustaining injury as road accident by motorcycle and same information was sent by hospital.
In the accident appellant suffered fracture in tibia and fibula bone of right leg and also fracture of 5th right metatarsal bone.
On the basis of information sent from hospital, after investigation by police, involvement of offending vehicle was found and FIR was registered accordingly.
In the accident, appellant suffered 32% permanent disablement and his income so assessed is on the lower side.
She further prayed that in case this Court finds any substance in the appeal, then amount of award be calculated as per her pleadings in appeal.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent No. 1 submitted that as the vehicle was insured on the date of accident, if this Court finds that appellant is entitled to receive compensation then respondent No. 2 Insurance Company is liable to make the payment of compensation amount.
5. Learned counsel for respondent no. 2 Insurance Company supported the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the record.
7.

From perusal of record as well as evidence brought on record, it is clear that the report which was sent to police by the hospital, there is clear mention of receiving such injuries in a road accident in which appellant suffered fracture of tibia and fibula bone of right leg and also fracture in 5th metatarsal bone.
On the basis of report sent from hospital, police investigated the matter and found involvement of the offending vehicle and accordingly registered the FIR as is clear from the charge-sheet.

Appellant specifically in his evidence stated in respect of accident which is not rebutted as in rebuttal no evidence has been produced as such in the opinion of this Court, learned Claims Tribunal erred in rejecting the claim of the appellant.

8. As regards extent of permanent disability sustained by appellate, the disability certificate Ex.
P/46 as produced by the appellant is not believable,
As the disability certificate is silent whether the extent of disability @32% is in respect of whole body or only the leg ?.
Further on what basis and investigation the disability certificate is issued is not clear.

2 9.

sentences.text: As regards quantum of compensation

, in the opinion of this Court looking to the nature of injuries, evidence brought on record and documents produced, the amount of Rs. 99,763/- as calculated by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and needs no interference however,

same is rounded to Rs. 1 Lac.
10.

Accordingly, in light of the above discussion, the appeal filed by appellant is allowed in part and while setting aside the impugned award rejecting the claim of appellant, appellant is held entitled to receive a compensation of Rs. 1 Lac from respondent Insurance Company with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim case i.e. 8/3/2017.

Let the payment of compensation amount be made to the appellant alongwith interest within two months from today.
(ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY) JUDGE JPS/-
